page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v5 is a general-purpose instance built on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor within the x86_64 architecture. The server provisions 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It includes 256 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with support for cryptographic acceleration including AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. It does not include integrated GPUs or local storage disks, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent disk access.

Benchmark testing demonstrates strong multi-threaded compute capabilities across diverse workloads. The instance achieved an upper-quartile stress-ng multi-core metric of 86388.11 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17647.0, supported by fast software compilation results in Clang. Memory subsystems performed favorably, recording a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3100.34 and reaching over 63 million Redis SET operations per second. However, large uncached memory bandwidth tests placed the instance in the middle tier, and single-threaded operations exhibited moderate rather than exceptional throughput.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the instance provides high compute and memory density without the overhead of unused accelerator hardware or fixed local storage. The absence of local disk drives requires architectural planning around remote storage throughput and IOPS limits. Additionally, the processor lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions, which bounds performance on heavy vectorized tasks. The server is well aligned for distributed container platforms, large-scale CI/CD build environments, in-memory key-value caching, and transactional database backends backed by cloud block storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D64as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 32-core AMD EPYC 7763 processor delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs at up to 3.525 GHz. Configured with 256 GB of RAM, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory profile suitable for diverse enterprise tasks. Because it provisions without bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, workloads rely on remote managed disks, providing state detachment beneficial for horizontally orchestrated infrastructure. Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, reflected in high stress-ng metrics, fast Clang compilation rates, and top-tier PassMark memory performance. In-memory data structures benefit from throughput demonstrated by over 63 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking AVX-512 extensions, the instance avoids specialized vector compute in favor of cost-efficient resource density for continuous integration build farms, containerized microservices, relational databases, and high-throughput application servers.
